title: Extinction of Australian species
titleCn: 澳大利亚物种灭绝与濒危动物保护

paragraphs.text: You will hear a talk given by a specialist at a zoo about the implications of the extinction of species.
First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty on page seven.
Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.
Good afternoon. From my work as curator at the Brisbane Zoo, it is becoming increasingly obvious to me that the animal world is a highly endangered one.
It sometimes seems as though a new species is added to the endangered list every day, and a great deal of this is due to human activity.
You may have read about the orange-bellied parrot colonies in South Australia. These are under threat from wind farms. So even our attempts to save energy can have a negative impact.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text:
further example is provided by the expansion of our cities. Here in Australia, many species of frog are losing their habitat as a direct result of this urban development. What's more, thanks to the increasing use of pesticides, fewer insects are surviving.

00:02:10,960

Many species depend upon these as a food source, birds in particular, and so their numbers are declining as well.

00:02:19,700

So even in rural areas, we are having a damaging effect on species. In fact, when our farmers choose to grow large amounts of one staple crop each year, corn is a perfect example, this often results in the greater need for chemicals and fertilizers, which has a devastating effect on local wildlife.

00:02:42,000

Clearly, something needs to be done about this. However, very little can be achieved without full public support, and our general attitude is not always a positive one. Of course, it is easy to get people interested in animals such as the panda. Thanks to the attention it is given in the media, people are very aware of its plight and so are willing to give a great deal of support. However, it is not so easy to attract sympathy for those essential smaller species such as insects. They may seem insignificant, but these tiny creatures have an enormous effect on our ecosystem. And it isn't only size that is a problem when it comes to our attitude towards animals. There are certain animals that we would prefer to simply ignore for various reasons. Firstly, we might do this because of fear. That is the normal reaction when people see a shark or a snake, for example. Another reason might be that we believe that certain animals are rivals when it comes to food. Locusts and even mice could come into this category.

00:03:51,860

Then there are animals that we view with disgust because of how they look or feel. The many different parasites, for example.

00:04:00,350

We were there in Paris. Exclusive events and incredible restaurants.

00:04:10,040

Nights at the Sapphire Lounge on the set. Heaven.

00:04:12,920

Experience the world as an insider from exclusive lounges to immersive dining experiences, all with Chase Sapphire Reserve.

00:04:22,680

You may well ask, what does it matter if any of these species dies? Extinction is a fact of life, after all.

00:04:39,820

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text:
would argue that there are several reasons to be concerned about the extinction of any species.

00:04:46,600

Each species helps us to understand more about how our ecosystem works.

00:04:52,860

One species can be linked to many others in the food chain, for example.

00:04:57,740

And inevitably, they all lead back to us in some way.

00:05:03,160

We now know that the more complex the ecosystem is, the more stable it is. When this is the case, large numbers of one animal are quickly controlled by outbreaks of its predators.

00:05:16,840

We've also begun to realize that the presence or absence of certain plants can alert us to changes in our environment.

00:05:25,780

One type of plant might indicate the presence of rich mineral deposits. Another might alert us to toxic water.

00:05:34,520

And so even seemingly insignificant species can be helpful and beneficial to us.

00:05:40,960

This is especially true in the area of medicine.

00:05:44,940

There are many well-documented cases of the health benefits of pet ownership, especially with the ill or the handicapped. But not many people know that spiders are also being used in medicine.

00:05:59,000

The cobwebs they make can be used to assist with certain blood disorders.

00:06:04,660

It actually helps blood to clot.

00:06:08,340

Imagine how much more there is for us still to discover from plants and animals. But we can only do this if we can save these creatures from extinction.

00:06:19,000

Perhaps in the end, it is our self-interest that will save the animals.

00:06:28,160

That is the end of part four.

00:06:31,640

You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.
